status: Calibration-and-fold-gate batch complete: three single-device closings land together. (1) The host fold gate moved into the evidence layer so the no-HIP config test pins it on the same constants the kernels use; the audit found and fixed a real weakness first — the old weights {1, 2^32, 2^32, 2^32, -3*2^32} shared one value across ranks 1-3, so a duplicated row between two same-weight ranks was invisible to the fold identity. The new weights are pairwise distinct ODD numbers {1, 3, 5, 7, 2^64-15} summing to 1 mod 2^64: odd multiplication is a bijection on 64-bit words, so flipping ANY bit of any partial (a power-of-two weight would shift high bits out of the word) changes the fold, and distinctness makes a duplicated row visible for every rank pair. The gate is all-or-nothing: every word is verified before the first write, so a rejected fold leaves no partial result. The live nonfinite_reduction_gate case now injects a high-bit flip alongside the quiet-NaN pattern. (2) The clock64 calibration method, previously a throwaway in /tmp, is now the in-repo HIP-gated tool tq-clock-rate: per visible device, five fixed-tick spin passes timed by the host steady clock with an event-poll wall deadline; three independent runs on this machine measure median 2320.1-2320.4 MHz, re-deriving the 2.3 GHz anchor behind WAIT_BUDGET_TICKS. The operator runs it first on the five-card machine to re-check the margin assumption (slower clocks only add margin). (3) The bench fold bandwidth was a best-of-two single sample dominated by scheduling noise; it is now summarized over 32 passes with min/median/p90/max like every other measurement (measured min/median spread ~1.6x shows the old single number was not stable).
